Simulate panel data for child-penalty estimation

Source: R/simulate_data.R
simulate_data.Rd

Generates a balanced panel of annual earnings with life-cycle growth, a gender gap, selection on the timing of first birth, and gendered effects of parenthood, for trying out the estimators.

Usage

simulate_data(n_individuals = 10000, treatment_groups = 24:28, seed = 42)

Arguments

n_individuals

Whole number \(\ge 2\). Number of individuals (default 10 000), half of them women (rounded).

treatment_groups

Whole numbers \(\ge 21\): ages at first birth (default 24:28). Ages run from 20 to max(treatment_groups) - 1, so the largest group is never observed treated and serves only as a control.

seed

Whole number or NULL. RNG seed (default 42). The caller's RNG state is saved and restored on exit, so calling this function does not alter the global random stream; set.seed() before the call has no effect unless seed = NULL, which draws from the current RNG state.

Value

A balanced long panel (data.frame), n_individuals x (max(treatment_groups) - 20) rows sorted by id and age, with columns id, female (1 = female), age, D (age at first birth) and Y (earnings, positive).

Details

Earnings of person \(i\) at age \(a\) are $$\log Y_{i,a} = \mu_0 + \lambda D_i + \alpha_i + \beta_1 (a - 20) + \beta_2 (a - 20)^2 + \kappa F_i + \tau_f F_i 1\{a \ge D_i\} + \tau_m (1 - F_i) 1\{a \ge D_i\} + \varepsilon_{i,a},$$ with \(F_i = 1\) for women, \(\mu_0 = 10\), \(\lambda = 0.03\), \(\beta_1 = 0.08\), \(\beta_2 = -0.003\), \(\kappa = -0.10\), \(\tau_f = -0.30\), \(\tau_m = -0.05\), a permanent effect \(\alpha_i \sim N(0, 0.20^2)\) and a transitory shock \(\varepsilon_{i,a} \sim N(0, 0.15^2)\). The age at first birth \(D_i\) is drawn uniformly from treatment_groups, independently of gender and \(\alpha_i\); \(\lambda D_i\) makes later first births earn more at every age (selection on timing).

True values, the same for every treatment group and age after first birth: \(\theta(f) = e^{-0.30} - 1 = -0.259\), \(\theta(m) = e^{-0.05} - 1 = -0.049\), gap \(-0.210\); counterfactual gender earnings ratio \(\rho(\infty) = e^{-0.10} = 0.905\), observed ratio \(\rho(d) = 0.705\), effect of parenthood on the ratio \(\rho(d) - \rho(\infty) = -0.200\); parenthood's share of the gender gap 0.678. Because \(\lambda D_i\) scales earnings levels by group, parallel trends in levels (DID-PT) and TD-PT fail, while NTD-PT, TD-PR and TD-E-LOGS hold.

See also

multiple_treatment_group_analysis

Examples

# \donttest{
sim <- simulate_data(n_individuals = 2000)
head(sim)
#>   id female age  D        Y
#> 1  1      1  20 24 40643.68
#> 2  1      1  21 24 36525.46
#> 3  1      1  22 24 39327.60
#> 4  1      1  23 24 34390.98
#> 5  1      1  24 24 46404.27
#> 6  1      1  25 24 46884.98
range(sim$age)
#> [1] 20 27
# }
